parts.text: A student investigates the image formed by a converging lens. The apparatus is set up as shown in Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) The student: • switches on the lamp • places the lens a distance u = 20.0 cm from the illuminated object (a triangular hole in the card) • adjusts the position of the screen until a sharp image of the illuminated object is formed on the screen. Measure on Fig. 3.1, to the nearest 0.1 cm, the image distance d from the centre of the lens to the screen. d = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Fig. 3.1 is drawn to a scale of one‑fifth ( 1 5 ) full size. Calculate the actual image distance v from the lens and record your value in Table 3.1. Table 3.1 object distance u / cm image distance v / cm 20.0 25.0 37.2 35.0 26.5 45.0 22.7 55.0 20.9 60.0 20.2 [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The diagram in Fig. 3.2 shows the illuminated object and its image drawn full size when u = 20.0 cm.

ms.label: 3(b)(i)
ms.text:
image is inverted / upside down and
image is bigger / magnified

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The magnification m of the image can be calculated using the equation shown. m = v u Use your answer to (a)(ii) to calculate the magnification m of the image. m = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student repeats the procedure in (a)(i) for values of u = 25.0 cm, u = 35.0 cm, u = 45.0 cm, u = 55.0 cm and u = 60.0 cm. The student’s results are shown in Table 3.1. Plot a graph of v / cm (y‑axis) against u / cm (x‑axis). Draw the best‑fit curve. [3] 0 10 0 10 20 30 40 50 60 20 30 40 50 60

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
axes labelled with units
plots correct to ± ½ small square
good best-fit curve judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Use your graph to find the value of v when u = 30.0 cm. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. v = ................................................... cm [2]

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
method shown on graph
candidate’s value of v for u = 30.0 cm read correctly from the graph to ± ½ small square

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) The focal length f of the lens can be found using the equation f = uv (u + v) . Use the values of u and v from (d) to calculate the focal length of the lens. f = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text: f in the range 14.0 (cm) to 16.0 (cm) inclusive

ms.label: 3(f)
ms.text: move screen slowly / to and fro (owtte) / carry out experiment in a darkened part of the laboratory / use a brighter object
